public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim says LLMs were still hallucinating as of late 2025. In November 2025, Vectara's new leaderboard found that frontier models such as GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Grok-4 and DeepSeek-R1 hallucinated in more than 10% of summaries. Even the best model scored 3.3%. In September 2025, OpenAI researchers wrote that hallucinations persist even in state-of-the-art systems. No evidence shows any frontier model had eliminated them. That supports the observable part of the claim. The stronger idea that LLMs can never stop hallucinating is not tested here. The same OpenAI paper argues hallucinations could be reduced by changing evaluation incentives.
limitations: The Vectara benchmark measures faithfulness in summarization only, using its own detection model.
This grade covers persistence of hallucination in late 2025, not the claim that it can never be fixed.
The primary sources on newer models (for example the GPT-5.2 system card) could not be read.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post date, current LLMs, including frontier models, still produce hallucinations (plausible but false content) at measurable, non-trivial rates, and no model has eliminated them.

The phrase 'can't stop' also hints at an inherent, permanent limit. That stronger theoretical point cannot be settled by observation. This assessment checks only the observable part: whether hallucination persisted in state-of-the-art models in late 2025.
criteria.support_condition: Independent benchmarks or developer research from late 2025 show that leading LLMs still hallucinate at non-trivial rates.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence from late 2025 shows that frontier LLMs had reliably eliminated hallucinations, with near-zero rates across standard factuality and faithfulness tests.
